Hi, I'm new to lean and this time I want to learn it for real (after several attempts in the past years).

I have two projects for now:

  • Submitted a conjecture to formal conjectures: #Formal conjectures > decision problems and `ComputablePred` This is about Turing-computability and we could use some input on how to best formalize these computability problems in lean.
  • I'm also trying to auto-formalize an old paper of mine with claude code working off the .tex source of the paper: https://github.com/tom111/BEI-lean

Regarding the problem with ComputablePred: seems like there is little usages of this so far in mathlib. Looks like @Mario Carneiro originally added this and can likely give feedback if it is applied correctly in FC#3495

The second project, formalization of binomial edge ideals makes heavy use of https://wuprover.github.io/groebner_proj/ by @Hagb (Junyu Guo), so also :wave: there.

Theorems 1.1 and 2.1 in the paper to be formalized are Gröbner basis statements that are proved with Buchberger's criterion.

Claude is faster making progress with the formalization than I am with understanding what is going on, but there was definitely some code import from your repository after I pointed claude at your work. It's a bit of a moving target.

Will have to refactor once Gröbner bases are in mathlib or I figure out how to depend on your project.

Thank you for using our work and letting us know! I have created a branch v4.28.0 for lean v4.28.0, and you can insert the following to your lakefile.toml to let your project depend on ours.

[[require]]
name = "groebner"
git = "https://github.com/WuProver/groebner_proj.git"
rev = "v4.28.0"

Some other comments:

  • If you want to avoid our new definition MonomialOrder.withBotDegree, you can use MonomialOrder.IsRemainder.isRemainder_iff_degree', which is the equivalence of the definition of MonomialOrder.IsRemainder based on withBotDegree and the definition based on MonomialOrder.degree
  • As Buchberger's Criterion over MvPolynomial σ k where k is a field, isGroebnerBasis_iff_subset_ideal_and_isRemainder_zero' and isGroebnerBasis_iff_isRemainder_sPolynomial_zero' don't require the hypothesis on the polynomial set that it contains only units. (Both of them are on MonomialOrder.IsGroebnerBasis namespace.)

Will have to refactor once Gröbner bases are in mathlib

Some parts of our project may be refactored before they get merged into Mathlib, which may still introduce breaking changes.
